title: Concurrent scorer windowing and token-scheduling for tail-latency reduction
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The reranking endpoint shows a long tail of p99 latency under mixed workloads. Root causes observed in traces: large token sequences in a single scoring request, blocking microbatch slots while waiting for slow scorer paths, and uneven KV cache hit distributions across shards. This ticket proposes a hybrid approach: 1) concurrent scorer windows that allow a request to split into bounded scoring windows processed in parallel on different microbatches, 2) a token-scheduling policy that caps per-request token consumption per microbatch and enforces progressive deadlines, and 3) a guarded fast-path for cached prefixes to bypass heavyweight scoring when quality is expected to be stable. Goals: reduce p99 latency by >=30% for mixed load, keep p50/p90 stable, and avoid >5% regression in rerank quality (NDCG@10) compared to baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture implemented: scorer windowing with deterministic reassembly of scores
Token scheduler limits default to 1024 tokens/request and split windows to max 256 tokens each
CI integration with synthetic load harness and golden prompts for quality checks
Prod canary shows p99 latency drop >=30% on the rerank route for 72h with no quality regression >5%
Feature flag gated rollout and automatic rollback on error/latency spike
experiments: A/B test using weighted routing: control=baseline scorer, treatment=concurrent-window scorer (30% traffic)
Synthetic replay using production traces to validate microbatch packing and per-request fairness
Quality eval suite: NDCG@10 and MRR on labeled rerank promptset (3k examples) run nightly during canary
rollout_plan: Stage 1: integration tests + perf harness (this sprint). Stage 2: internal dogfood on dev cluster with 5% traffic (2 days). Stage 3: canary in prod with 30% traffic for 72h; monitor p50/p90/p99, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and quality metrics. Stage 4: full rollout with gradual increase to 100% over 2 days if metrics stable. Rollback: disable feature flag and resume previous scheduler if p99 increases >20% or quality drops >5%.
notes: Design choice: use deterministic windowing so score order is identical to monolithic scoring for explainability; we will normalize by token counts to avoid bias on longer windows
Trade-off: parallel windows increase compute fragmentation and may raise peak GPU utilization. Mitigation: adaptive batch packing and short-lived window leases
Decision: default token cap set to 1024 after experiments showed diminishing returns beyond that on p99 improvement
Edge-case: single very long document (>4096 tokens) will be fallthrough to streaming scorer to avoid multi-window blowup
Follow-ups: explore KV-cache prefetch hints from query embeddings and a low-cost approximate scorer for early filtering
blockers: Need a small change in microbatch allocator to support heterogeneous window sizes (ENG-30110) - engineering owner assigned
Long-running PR review for kernel scheduling changes that affect priority preemption
